papers.title: HEAT TREATMENT OF TI-6AL-4V PRODUCED BY LASERCUSING
papers.abstract: LaserCUSING® is a selective laser melting (SLM) process that is capable of manufacturing parts by melting powder with heat input from a laser beam. LaserCUSING demonstrates potential for producing the intricate geometries specifically required for biomedical implants and aerospace applications. One main limitation to this form of rapid prototyping is the lack of published studies on the material performance of the resulting material. Studies of the material’s performance are often complicated by dependence on several factors, including starting powder properties, laser parameters, and post-processing heat treatments. This study aims to investigate the mechanical properties of LaserCUSING-produced Ti-6Al-4V and its performance relative to the conventional wrought counterpart. A combination of conventional and LaserCUSING-tailored heat treatments is performed. The resulting microstructures are studied and linked to the properties obtained from hardness tests. The findings highlight that LaserCused Ti-6Al-4V is competitive with traditional materials, provided that optimal parameters are chosen and parts are subject to tailored post-processing. In the as-built condition, LaserCused Ti-6Al-4V displays superior strength and hardness as a result of a martensitic microstructure, and a poorer performance in ductility. However, the material performance can be improved using tailored heat treatments. Careful consideration must be given to suitable post-processing before application in critical components in the aerospace or biomedical industry can occur
papers.venue: The South African Journal of Industrial Engineering

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了激光熔融Ti-6Al-4V的力学性能和热处理效果，但与多孔植入物、应力遮挡或骨整合无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include porous structures, stress shielding analysis, fatigue testing, or osseointegration evaluation, which are core to AM biomedical implants.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the mechanical properties of LaserCusing-produced Ti-6Al-4V and the effect of post-processing heat treatments.
summary_en.method: A combination of conventional and tailored heat treatments were applied, and microstructures were correlated with hardness and mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: Tailored heat treatments improved ductility while maintaining high strength, making the material competitive with wrought counterparts.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (hardness and tensile properties) and microstructural analysis.
